# Data Generator

## Description

Source component that generates records via a CTL2 (or Java) `generate()` transformation. It has no input ports and one or more output ports. Common for synthesizing test/mock datasets, generating sequence-driven streams, or fanning records to multiple outputs (paired with PARTITION).

> **Name vs type:** the type string is `DATA_GENERATOR`.

## Purpose & when to use

Reach for DATA_GENERATOR when:
- You need synthetic / mock data for testing or scaffolding (random names, dates, amounts).
- You're generating a fixed or variable-length stream computed from sequences, parameters, or random functions.
- You want to fan records to multiple outputs based on the transform's return value (`return 0`, `return 1`, etc.).

Don't use DATA_GENERATOR when:
- The data exists in a file or database → use the appropriate reader.
- You only need a single seed token for a jobflow → use GET_JOB_INPUT.

## XML template

```xml
<Node id="GEN0" type="DATA_GENERATOR" recordsNumber="500"
      guiX="100" guiY="100">
  <attr name="generate"><![CDATA[//#CTL2 — see ## CTL2 contract]]></attr>
</Node>
```

- `type="DATA_GENERATOR"`.
- Mandatory attribute: `recordsNumber`.
- One of `generate` / `generateURL` / `generateClass` is **required** (the CTL2 body is anchored in the `generate` `<attr>` CDATA).
- Output metadata is not auto-propagated — declare a `<Metadata>` block per output edge.

## Properties

| Property | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `recordsNumber` | yes | — | How many records to generate. **Set this to the exact count you want — it is the way to control output volume.** |
| `generate` | yes* | — | Inline CTL2 generator with a `generate()` function. *One of `generate`, `generateURL`, `generateClass` required. |
| `generateURL` | yes* | — | Path to an external `.ctl` file. |
| `generateClass` | yes* | — | Java class implementing `RecordGenerate`. |
| `charset` | no | — | Charset used when reading generator source from `generateURL`. Not used with `generateClass`. |
| `randomFields` | no | — | **Deprecated.** Legacy record-pattern random field configuration; use CTL2 random functions in `generate()` instead. |
| `sequenceFields` | no | — | **Deprecated.** Legacy record-pattern sequence mapping; use CTL2 `sequence(Name).next()` in `generate()` instead. |
| `randomSeed` | no | — | Legacy random seed for pattern/random-field generation. For CTL2, prefer `setRandomSeed(seed)` in `init()` or `preExecute()`. |
| `pattern` | no | — | **Deprecated.** Legacy record-pattern configuration; use CTL2 in `generate()` instead. |

### Random function reference

CTL2 helpers commonly used inside `generate()`:

| Function | Returns |
|---|---|
| `randomInteger(min, max)` | integer in [min, max] |
| `randomLong(min, max)` | long |
| `randomDouble()` | double in [0.0, 1.0) |
| `randomString(minLen, maxLen)` | random-letter string |
| `randomBoolean()` | boolean |
| `randomDate(from, to, format)` | date in range |
| `randomUUID()` | UUID string |
| `setRandomSeed(seed)` | repeatable runs (call from `init()` or `preExecute()`) |

## Input & output metadata

No inputs (source — `$in.0` is not available); one or more outputs, each can have different metadata (multi-port generation: `generate()`'s integer return value selects the destination port). Nothing is auto-propagated — define a `<Metadata>` block for every output edge.

```
auto_propagated_metadata: none   # source — you define every output <Metadata> AND populate it in generate() (CTL2)
```

## CTL2 contract

The component's CTL2 entry point is `generate()`. (Superset of the in-code `CTLAuthorComponentContractKb` `DATAGENERATOR` blob.)

**(a) Entry-point signature — verbatim, exact:**

```ctl
function integer generate()
```

**(b) Lifecycle / call order:**
- `generate()` is called repeatedly — `recordsNumber` times. **Set `recordsNumber` to the number of records you want; it is what bounds the run.**
- Optional lifecycle hooks (run once per run unless noted): `init()`, `preExecute()`, `postExecute()`, plus the `generateOnError` recovery handler.

**(c) Port model:**
- **No input port** — there is no `$in.0`; generate from module-level state, constants, sequences, and random functions.
- Writes generated records to one or more output ports (`$out.0`, `$out.1`, …).

**(d) Return semantics & idioms — keep in mind:**
- Return values from `generate()`:
  - `ALL` / `OK` / `0` — emit on port 0.
  - an integer port number — emit on that port (multi-port generation).
  - `SKIP` — drop this record (does **not** count against `recordsNumber`).
  - `STOP` — stops generation immediately, but is treated as an **abort, not a graceful end-of-stream**. It is an advanced way to control the ending from CTL; **prefer bounding the run with `recordsNumber`** for normal use.
- Module-level counters / state are expected here (unlike most transforms) — declare them at module scope and increment across calls.
- `++` is valid on module/local variables in DATA_GENERATOR CTL (it is the natural way to advance a counter).
- For sequence values, use `sequence(Name).next()`.
- For repeatable test fixtures, call `setRandomSeed(seed)` from `init()` or `preExecute()`.

**(e) Minimal correct skeleton:**

```ctl
//#CTL2
integer i = 0;
function integer generate() {
    $out.0.id = i;        // recordsNumber on the node bounds the count
    i++;
    return OK;
}
```

**(f) Canonical mistake:**
- Wrong: expecting `$in.0` inside DATA_GENERATOR — there is no input port.
- Correct: generate from module-level state, constants, sequences, and random functions.

**Optional lifecycle functions:**

```ctl
function boolean init() { /* setup */ return true; }
function void preExecute()  { /* per-run setup */ }
function void postExecute() { /* per-run teardown */ }
function integer generateOnError(string errorMessage, string stackTrace) {
    // recover from generate() failure
    return SKIP;
}
```

## Examples

### Minimal — random sales records

```xml
<Node id="GEN0" type="DATA_GENERATOR" recordsNumber="500">
  <attr name="generate"><![CDATA[//#CTL2
function integer generate() {
    $out.0.branch_id   = (sequence(SEQ0).next() % 10) + 1;
    $out.0.product     = randomString(5, 10);
    $out.0.quantity    = randomInteger(1, 50);
    $out.0.unit_price  = randomDouble() * 100;
    $out.0.sale_date   = today();
    return ALL;
}
]]></attr>
</Node>
```

### Full — fan-out to multiple files

Generate 500 records, distribute across 10 output files keyed by `branch_id`. The canonical CloverDX pattern is **writer-side partitioning** — one writer configured with a partition key and `#` placeholder in the output file path. PARTITION-the-component is **not** needed for fan-out by key.

#### Preferred — writer-side partitioning (one writer, N files)

```xml
<Node id="GEN0" type="DATA_GENERATOR" recordsNumber="500">
  <attr name="generate"><![CDATA[//#CTL2
const string[] PRODUCTS = ["Rose","Tulip","Sunflower","Lily","Orchid","Daisy","Carnation","Lavender"];

function integer generate() {
    $out.0.branch_id   = (sequence(SEQ0).next() % 10) + 1;
    $out.0.product     = PRODUCTS[randomInteger(0, length(PRODUCTS) - 1)];
    $out.0.quantity    = randomInteger(1, 50);
    $out.0.unit_price  = randomDouble() * 100;
    return ALL;
}
]]></attr>
</Node>

<Node id="WRITER0" type="FLAT_FILE_WRITER"
      fileURL="${DATAOUT_DIR}/branches/branch_#.csv"
      partitionKey="branch_id"
      partitionFileTag="keyNameFileTag"
      outputFieldNames="true"
      makeDirs="true"/>

<Edge id="E0" fromNode="GEN0:0" toNode="WRITER0:0" metadata="Sales"/>
```

The `#` placeholder in the writer output path becomes each distinct `branch_id` value (`branch_1.csv` … `branch_10.csv`). One writer node, no PARTITION component, no manual N-port wiring. See `csv-file` § *Native file partitioning* for the full attribute reference.

#### Alternative — PARTITION component (only when each output needs different logic)

Reach for the PARTITION component **only** when each output port needs a genuinely different downstream — different metadata, different transform, different sink type. Don't use it just to split into N similar files.

```xml
<Node id="PART0" type="PARTITION">
  <attr name="partitionSource"><![CDATA[//#CTL2
function integer getOutputPort() {
    return $in.0.branch_id - 1;  // route to ports 0..9
}
]]></attr>
</Node>

<!-- Then N writers, one per port — different per-port transforms if that's why
     PARTITION exists in this graph. If they all write the same shape to similar
     files, use the writer-side partitioning pattern above instead. -->
```

> The PARTITION node uses its own CTL2 contract (`getOutputPort()`), distinct from DATA_GENERATOR's `generate()`. See `partition`.

## Common mistakes

- **`recordsNumber` not set** — required attribute; CheckConfig fails.
- **Forgetting output `<Metadata>`.** DATA_GENERATOR doesn't auto-propagate. Every output edge needs explicit metadata.
- **Relying on `STOP` for a clean finish.** `STOP` stops generation but counts as an abort, not a graceful end. Control how many records are produced with `recordsNumber`; reserve `STOP` for advanced cases.
- **Random values per run breaking tests.** Set `setRandomSeed(42)` in `init()` for repeatable test fixtures.
- **Multi-port generation without metadata-per-port.** Each output port needs its own `<Metadata>` block; the transform's `return N` selects the destination.
- **Expecting `$in.0` in `generate()`.** DATA_GENERATOR has no input port — generate from module state, constants, sequences, and random functions.
